title: How to Meet New People in College (Without It Feeling Awkward)
description: Practical ways to meet new people in college — clubs, fests, hostels, and online — plus how to turn a quick chat into a real friendship or date.
blocks: College is supposed to be the easiest time of your life to meet people. But between classes, assignments and the same group you met in first year, it often doesn’t feel that way. Here’s what actually works.
1. Join one club for the people, not the CV

Pick a club where you’ll see the same faces every week — a dramatics society, a sports team, a music or quiz club. Repeated, low-pressure time together is how most friendships (and relationships) start.
2. Say yes to fests and events — and go alone sometimes
When you’re with your usual group, you talk to your usual group. Going to a talk, an open mic or a fest event on your own makes it far easier to start conversations with new people.
“Is this your first time at this fest?”
“How did you find the last quiz round?”
Specific questions are easier to answer than “hi”, and they give the other person something to talk about.

Most connections die after the first chat. If you enjoyed talking to someone, suggest something concrete: a chai after class, studying together, or the next event. Swap Instagram handles so you can follow up.
5. Try meeting beyond your own circle

Apps built for students can help you meet people from other departments and nearby colleges. On DateU, you can join a curated matching round or have a 5-minute voice call with someone new — no photos, no pressure — and keep chatting only if you both want to.
Meeting people is mostly about showing up regularly, being curious, and following up. Start with one of these this week.

title: Online Dating Safety Tips for College Students
description: Stay safe while dating online: protect your personal info, spot fake profiles, meet safely the first time, and know when to block and report.
blocks: Dating apps can be a great way to meet people outside your circle — as long as you stay in control. These simple habits make a big difference.
Keep personal details private at first
Don’t share your phone number, address, hostel room or class timetable early on.
Keep chatting inside the app until you’re comfortable.
Be careful with photos that show where you live or study.
Only one photo, or photos that look like a model shoot.
Pushing to move to WhatsApp or Telegram immediately.
Any request for money, gift cards, OTPs or “help with a payment”. Report it straight away.
On DateU, students can verify their college ID, and verified profiles show a blue badge.
A short voice call tells you a lot about someone. DateU’s random calls are voice-only and last 5 minutes, so you can get a feel for a person before sharing anything.
Meet in a busy public place — a campus café or a popular spot nearby.
Tell a friend where you’re going and who you’re meeting.
Arrange your own way there and back.
Leave whenever you feel uncomfortable. You never owe anyone your time.
If someone makes you uncomfortable, block and report them. On DateU it takes one tap from the chat menu, reports are confidential, and our team reviews every one.

title: How to Make Your Dating Profile Stand Out
description: Simple ways to write a better bio, choose photos that work, and pick interests that start conversations — so you get more matches.
blocks: In a curated round, people only see a handful of profiles — so each one gets real attention. A few small changes make yours much easier to like.
Make your first photo a clear, well-lit shot of your face — no sunglasses, no group.
Add at least one photo doing something you enjoy: sport, music, travel, a hobby.
Skip heavy filters. People want to recognise you when you meet.
“I love travel and music” describes almost everyone. Try something specific that invites a reply:
“Currently trying to find the best momos near campus — accepting recommendations.”
“Will beat you at Codenames. Bad at cooking, good at chai.”
Pick interests you could talk about for ten minutes. They show up on your card and give people an easy first message.
A verified badge tells people you’re a real student. On DateU you can upload your college ID from the Profile tab — only our team sees it.
Join rounds when they go live and reply to matches quickly. Active profiles simply get more conversations.

title: Easy First Date Ideas for College Students in Delhi
description: Low-pressure, budget-friendly first date ideas in Delhi for students — cafés, walks, markets and activities that make conversation easy.
blocks: The best first dates are short, public and easy to talk through. Here are student-friendly ideas around Delhi that don’t need a big budget.
Grab a coffee at a café near your campus and then take a walk. Walking side by side makes conversation feel natural, and it’s easy to end or extend.
Places like Hauz Khas Village, Khan Market, Kamla Nagar or Sarojini Nagar give you plenty to look at and talk about — and street food to share.
Lodhi Garden, Sunder Nursery and Hauz Khas lake are great for an afternoon. Many monuments have student-friendly entry fees.
A campus fest or open-mic night
A museum or art gallery on a weekday
Plan for about an hour, meet somewhere public, and split the bill or take turns. If it goes well, you’ll have an easy reason to plan a second date.
